messages.author: 7f1bd60f28c4e54c
messages.subject: Linkage mapping
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm new to R/QTL and linkage mapping in general, so please bear with
me. I'm having problems using rqtl to assemble linkage maps using a
snp dataset containing 7327 snp loci that segregate among 20 progeny
of a female informative backcross (the female is the f1 of an
interspecific cross). My complete dataset is actually ~9300 snps for
30 progeny but I filtered out some individuals and loci that had large
amounts of missing data. Using the reduced dataset, 91% of genotypes
are present. I should mention that the female-informative cross was
intentional as there is no recombination during oogenesis in these
species meaning that any loci on the same chromosome will be
completely linked.

I've been using the tutorial to go through the process of assigning
loci to LGs but when I get to the formlinkagegroups step the
distribution of the loci end up being highly skewed so that a large
portion end up on one LG and each of the remaining loci appear singly
on other LGs (i've tried a range of different max.rf values and
min.lod scores). It doesn't make sense to have ~6000 snps on one LG
and ~1300 others all on different LGs. Also, there should only be 30
LGs. The potential issues I run into along the way are an initial
warning stating that "some chromosomes > 1000 cM...", a lot of
duplicate markers during the finddupmarkers step (which I haven't
filtered out because the tutorial doesn't cover this and I haven't
read into rqtl enough), and i get a about 30 or so loci that may have
switched alleles during the checkalleles step (after using markerlrt
but not with est.rf). Also, the frequency of homozygote genotypes is
about 3x as much as the frequency of heterozygote genotypes giving a
3:1 ratio (this should be about a 1:1 for a backcross).

I initially assumed that the issue was due to the segregation
distortion I was seeing in the genotype frequencies but after using an
even further reduced dataset of ~2000 loci that were selected for
their more even ratio of homozygotes to heterozygotes, I still
encounter the problem.

Currently, I'm at a loss as I do not know how to proceed.

Any help would be wonderful!

Thanks,

Bryan

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Linkage mapping
parts:
It seems unlikely that you would be able to generate a genetic map with just 20 meioses.
The possible recombination fractions between two markers are just 0/20, 1/20, 2/20, ...

karl
